main_text.head: LIBER QVINTVS. FINIVM REGVNDORVM.
TITVLVS I.
main_text.p: CVM siticulosa admodum esset terra Attica, vt testatur Dicaearchus ἐν τῷ βίῳ τῆς Ἑλλάδος. ἡ δὲ πόλις, ξηρὰ πᾶσα οὖσα ὕδατος[?], nec perennes essent amnes, aut fontes multi, aut lacus, ita vt oporteret puteos effodere: Legem hac de re scripsit Solon, qua cauit licere publico vti puteo, si intra hippicum sit: vbi maius esset interuallum, priuatum sibi foderent puteum.
Οπου μὲν ἔστι δημόσιον φρέαρ ἐντὸς ἱππικοῦ, χρῆσθαι τούτῳ· ὅπου δὲ πλεῖον ἀπέχῃ, ἕκαστῳ ὕδωρ ἰδίῳ[?].

p.i: Publico puteo, qui intra hippicum sit, vtuntor: si maius sit interuallum, priuatum sibi quisque effodiunto.

main_text.p: Legem hanc habet Plutarchus in Solone: ἐπὶ δὲ ταῖς ὕδωρ, ὅτε ποταμοῖς ἔστιν ἀεὶ ὕδωρ, ὅτε λίμναις ἔχοιεν, ὅτ' ἀφόνοις πηγὰς ἢ χώρα ξηρὰ ἀρχῆς, ἀλλ' οἱ πλεῖστοι φρέα- σιν ποιητοῖς ἐχρῶντο, νόμον ἔθεντο. Οπου μὲν ἔστι δημόσιον φρέαρ ἐντὸς ἱππικοῦ, χρῆσθαι τούτῳ (τὸ δὲ ἱππικὸν ἀξέσημα, πεντάρων τῷ σταδίων.) ὅπου δὲ πλεῖον ἀπέχῃ, ἕκαστῳ ὕδωρ ἰδίῳ[?]. Hippicum interuallum est stadiorum quatuor, vt inquit Plutarchus. Hesychius vnius tantum stadii facit, ἱππικόν, ὅ ἐστι στάδιον. Quod equidem praetulerim notatione nominis: nam videtur esse illud interuallum, quod sine vlla intermissione equus conficit & decurrit. Temere tamen non licebat intra fines suos sibi puteum fodere, sed ὀργυιὰς latitudinem ab alieno fundo oportebat relinquere ex hac Solonis Lege:
ΕΑΝ ΤΙΣ ΦΡΕΑΡ ΠΑΡ' ΑΛΛΟ-ΤΡΙΩΙ ΧΩΡΙΩΙ ΟΡΥΤΤΗΙ ΟΡ-ΓΥΙΑΝ ΑΠΟΛΙΠΕΙΝ.

p.i: Si quis puteum iuxta alterius agrum fodiat, orgyæ spadium relinquito.

main_text.p: Meminit huius Legis καὶ ἀΒλεξὲι descripsit Gaius Libro IV. ad Legem XII. Tabularum, & Solonis fuisse docet. Sciendum est, in actione finium regundorum illud obseruandum esse, quod ad exemplum quodammodo eius Legis scriptum est, quam Athenis Solon dicitur tulisse: nam illis ita est: ΕΑΝ ΤΙΣ ΦΡΕΑΡ ΠΑΡ' ΑΛΛΟΤΡΙΩΙ ΧΩΡΙΩΙ ΩΡΥΤΤΗΙ ΟΡΓΥΙΑΝ ΑΠΟΛΙΠΕΙΝ. Lege XIII.

page.notes: Greek text is printed in a small, worn type; the Greek readings marked [?] are doubtful. The Greek of the Plutarch quotation ("ἐπὶ δὲ ταῖς ... νόμον ἔθεντο") and the Hesychius gloss are only partly legible and should be checked against the scan. Parallel Greek and Latin columns are transcribed one after the other: Greek first, then the Latin translation. The first Greek line of the opening paragraph ("ὕδατος") is doubtful. The initial C is decorative and is joined to "VM" as "CVM". The Greek in the Solon quotation is printed in mixed type, and some words are unclear.
